security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, OMERO object IDs, or reference URLs. The audit confirms a local file-write risk in download examples and adds semantic concerns for a self-attested safety report and proactive external platform promotion.

remediation.issue: Self-authored audit result is packaged with the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation_result.json from the distributed skill or label it as non-authoritative test data that agents must ignore.

remediation.issue: Download examples write server-provided filenames to local paths.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize filenames, strip path separators, normalize paths, and verify every resolved path remains inside the chosen download directory.

remediation.issue: The skill promotes an external hosted platform during complex workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic promotion or require explicit user consent before recommending external services for sensitive research data.

remediation.issue: Administrative examples include impersonation and owner-changing operations.
remediation.suggestion: Mark admin-only examples with clear authorization, audit logging, and institutional policy requirements.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Remote Filenames Used For Local Downloads
semantic_findings.description: Download examples join OMERO-provided file names directly with local directories before writing files. Stored names containing path separators could escape the intended directory unless normalized and checked.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples derive file_path from server-side file names and then write bytes locally. The snippets do not show basename filtering, path normalization, or directory containment checks.

content.user_title: Access OMERO Microscopy Data With Python
content.value_statement: Microscopy teams need reliable ways to retrieve images, metadata, ROIs, and screening results from OMERO. This skill provides Python patterns for OMERO access, analysis, annotations, tables, and batch scripts.
actual_capabilities: Connect to OMERO servers with BlitzGateway examples and secure session cleanup.
Navigate projects, datasets, images, screens, plates, wells, and annotations.
Retrieve pixel data as NumPy arrays for image analysis workflows.
Create, read, and analyze ROIs and store measurements in OMERO tables.
Manage tags, key-value annotations, file annotations, and metadata namespaces.
Build OMERO.scripts patterns for server-side batch processing.
limitations: Requires an accessible OMERO server and valid credentials.
Provides code patterns; it does not supply a running OMERO instance.
Image analysis algorithms must come from user code or external libraries.
Administrative examples require OMERO privileges and local policy approval.

use_cases.title: Support Shared OMERO Data Access
use_cases.description: Guide users through project, dataset, image, and annotation retrieval for shared research repositories.

use_cases.title: Analyze Image Datasets
use_cases.description: Retrieve pixel data, inspect ROIs, calculate measurements, and store results back in OMERO.

use_cases.title: Build Batch OMERO Workflows
use_cases.description: Create repeatable server-side scripts and table outputs for screening and microscopy analysis pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Connect To OMERO
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a safe Python pattern for connecting to an OMERO server with environment variables and automatic cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: List Dataset Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me list all images in an OMERO dataset, include image names, identifiers, sizes, and basic error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Measure ROI Intensities
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow to retrieve ROIs from OMERO images, calculate intensity summaries, and prepare results for an OMERO table.

prompt_templates.title: Design Batch Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an OMERO.scripts workflow for processing a dataset, writing table results, handling failures, and cleaning up resources.

output_examples.input: How should I connect to OMERO and list my projects?
output: A connection checklist using BlitzGateway, environment-based credentials, secure transfer settings, and automatic session cleanup.
A project listing approach that handles failed connections and closes the session after use.
A short note explaining why credentials should not be hardcoded.

output_examples.input: I need intensity statistics for ROIs across one dataset.
output: A workflow that retrieves dataset images, reads existing ROI shapes, selects the requested channel, and calculates summary statistics.
A result plan with image identifiers, ROI identifiers, area, mean intensity, and quality warnings.
A storage recommendation for saving measurements in an OMERO table.

output_examples.input: Can I attach analysis results back to OMERO?
output: A metadata workflow for choosing tags, key-value annotations, file annotations, or tables based on result type.
Guidance for namespaces, object links, permission checks, and safe local file handling before upload.

best_practices: Use secure connections, context managers, and explicit cleanup for every OMERO session.
Store credentials in environment variables or approved secret stores, never in shared scripts.
Validate object IDs, group context, and permissions before reads, writes, deletes, or admin operations.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding OMERO credentials, hostnames, or privileged account details in notebooks or scripts.
Downloading server-provided filenames without sanitizing paths and checking directory containment.
Running broad batch queries without pagination, streaming, memory limits, or failure reporting.

faq.question: What is OMERO?
faq.answer: OMERO is an open-source platform for managing, viewing, and analyzing microscopy images and metadata.

faq.question: Do I need an OMERO server?
faq.answer: Yes. You need a reachable OMERO server, valid credentials, and permissions for the data you want to access.

faq.question: Which programming interface does this skill use?
faq.answer: It focuses on Python examples using omero-py and the BlitzGateway API.

faq.question: Can it process high-content screening data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for screens, plates, wells, image retrieval, measurements, and table outputs.

faq.question: Can it create or analyze ROIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers ROI shapes, intensity statistics, coordinate export, and result storage workflows.

faq.question: Does it include ready-made segmentation algorithms?
faq.answer: No. It shows how to access OMERO data, but analysis algorithms come from your code or imaging libraries.
